clue.text: Who's that MP who reportedly went for a nightly swim dad?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the words would be heard

blocks.clueFragment: went for a nightly swim dad
blocks.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont each night to visit Hero; his son would be Leander's son

explanation.surface: Someone half-remembers a story about an MP whose father took midnight dips.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee Anderson is the Reform UK MP for Ashfield; said aloud, his name sounds like 'Leander son', the child of the mythical nightly swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Anderson sits in the House of Commons, so he is an example of a Member of Parliament.

clue.text: Suffolk resort hol we arranged "the absolute pits"

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so these letters are laid out differently

blocks.note: a seaside town on the Suffolk coast, England's most easterly point
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumpy holidaymaker rates their Suffolk seaside break as dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The town's name runs straight into the phrase: LOWESTOFT supplies the first ten letters, including the T of THE. 'Hol' is British slang for holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for the very worst, the most contemptible level anything can sink to.

clue.text: Nurse, dizzy blonde, put in the House of Lords

definitions.text: put in the House of Lords

indicators.note: a dizzy person's head is spinning, so the letters of the next word are spun into a new order

blocks.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained nurse is unexpectedly given a peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to the peerage makes them a noble, which gives them a seat in the Lords.

clue.text: 1D Former Culture Minister I remember finally

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 1 down, LOWEST OF THE LOW

indicators.note: the former part of a name is its front, so only the opening of the minister's first name is kept
finally points to the very end of the word before it, so only its last letter is used

blocks.note: Nadine Dorries was Culture Secretary in 2021-22
taken as written
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a former Culture Minister as a low point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former' does double duty in the surface as 'ex-', but in the wordplay it keeps only the front of the first name, NAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, which is what the lowest of the low means.

clue.text: City sojourn, son packed gear

indicators.note: something packed is stuffed inside, so the son goes into the sojourn

blocks.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a sojourn is a temporary stay
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A city break where the son's luggage is crammed with kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' looks like luggage, but it is slang for drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is slang for illegal drugs, and ecstasy is one such drug, so this is definition by example.

clue.text: Told to go online to cover Cummings, in a state of thrall

indicators.note: what is told is spoken, so the answer piece is a word that sounds like the one meant
in a down entry one piece covers another by sitting directly on top of it

blocks.note: to surf is to browse the internet
Dominic Cummings, Boris Johnson's former chief adviser, known as Dom

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to browse the web for news on Dominic Cummings, as if enslaved.
explanation.definitionFit: Serfdom was the medieval condition of a bonded labourer, and thrall is an old word for bondage.

clue.text: Scrubs 30p lettuce?

blocks.note: surface reading: a shopping list or price tag for cleaning gear and cheap salad
setter's reading: three informal labels, for Wormwood Scrubs prison, for the MP Lee Anderson and for the lettuce that outlasted Liz Truss

explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a London prison, '30p Lee' became Lee Anderson's tag after he said meals could be cooked for 30p, and a tabloid's lettuce famously outlasted Truss's premiership. The question mark flags definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Each is an informal substitute label used in place of a proper name, which is what these words are.

clue.text: Inquiry exposed Jenrick

indicators.note: exposing something strips its covering, so the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: a probe is an investigation

explanation.surface: An investigation lays bare the conduct of the Tory politician Robert Jenrick.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Jenrick, Conservative MP and former minister, is known by the short form of his first name.

clue.text: Change political party

blocks.note: first meaning: to alter or improve
second meaning: the British party led by Nigel Farage

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a slogan calling for a new government; Reform UK is the right-wing party led by Nigel Farage.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to amend something, and as a proper noun it names a UK party.

clue.text: Beefy individual thumped controversial MP

blocks.note: to belt is to hit hard
George Galloway, the firebrand MP elected for Rochdale in 2024

explanation.surface: A burly man has punched a divisive politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beefy individual' looks like a muscular person, but it is one animal of a beef cattle breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belted Galloway is a Scottish breed of beef cattle with a white band round its middle.

clue.text: Opening with light blow that hurts!

blocks.note: a light wind is a gentle blow of air
OW is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: A boxer's first jab is light but still painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' and 'blow' suggest a boxing bout; the blow is a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is an aperture in a wall, and an opening can be any such gap.

clue.text: Kinkily clad figures - scandalous!

indicators.note: something kinky is twisted, so the following letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid shrieks about people in kinky outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe behaviour that is shocking and brings shame.

clue.text: Mountain rescuer stumped by Tory Jenkin

blocks.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
Sir Bernard Jenkin, Conservative MP

explanation.surface: An Alpine rescuer is baffled by a Conservative MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' reads as baffled, but in cricket a batter stumped is out, scored as 'st'.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Bernard is the large dog breed famed for finding travellers lost in Alpine snow.

clue.text: Tender shark

blocks.note: first meaning: one who tends the sick
second meaning: a bottom-dwelling shark species

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective, gentle or sore, set against a fierce shark; here it is a noun, one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse looks after patients, and the nurse shark is a sluggish species of warm seas.

clue.text: Discovered secret: party not right to spend money needlessly

indicators.note: dis-covered means its covers are taken off, so the outer letters go
not tells us the next item is to be taken away from the word before it

blocks.note: covert means hidden
taken as written
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A clandestine party is exposed, with the right shown to be wasting cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Overpaying means handing over more than something is worth, so the money is spent without need.

clue.text: Complains on GMB about old ecclesiastical music

indicators.note: about here means lying around in, so the letters are found scattered within the words before

blocks.note: inside comPLAINS ON G(MB)

explanation.surface: A viewer grumbles on breakfast TV about church chanting.
explanation.walkthrough: GMB is Good Morning Britain, an ITV breakfast show.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is the unaccompanied chant of the medieval Western church, also called plainchant.

clue.text: For now, against dropping internet fad

indicators.note: dropping something leaves it behind, so the word for against is taken out

blocks.note: for the meantime means for now
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: An online craze is being opposed, at least for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a joke or image copied and spread rapidly online, a typical web craze.

clue.text: Uninvited visitor at home tense, more vulgar

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
comparative of rude

explanation.surface: An unwanted guest arrives, making the household anxious and the talk coarser.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder enters a place without permission, unlike a welcome guest.

clue.text: See 8
"Suspend Jonathan Gullis" - constituents

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the letters are drawn from within the name

blocks.note: inside JonatHAN Gullis

explanation.surface: Voters demand that their MP Jonathan Gullis be suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' suggests the voters of Gullis's former Stoke seat; here it means component letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something is to suspend it from above.

clue.text: Split in ERG irritated CON man

indicators.note: an irritated person is worked up, so these letters are stirred into another order
in says the first piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a rift is a split or breach

explanation.surface: A rift in the Tory European Research Group angers a Conservative man.
explanation.walkthrough: The ERG is the Eurosceptic European Research Group of Tory MPs, and CON is short for Conservative; the capitals disguise a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A grifter is a swindler who works small-scale scams, the same as a confidence trickster.

clue.text: Chose Hannan? Without any restrictions?? (Makes exclamation to God)

indicators.note: restrictions are the limits at each end, so each word loses its outside letters

blocks.note: taken as written
Daniel Hannan, Tory peer and Brexit campaigner

explanation.surface: A puzzled aside asks whether the Brexiteer Hannan chose to scrap all limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a cry of praise or adoration addressed to God in Jewish and Christian worship.

clue.text: Rome house where Macron might be found topless?

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so losing the top drops it

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
the Elysée Palace is the French president's residence

explanation.surface: A Roman house where the French president might be spotted sunbathing topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome' stands for the papacy by metonymy, as in 'Rome has spoken'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the papal government, which is commonly referred to simply as Rome.

clue.text: See 1
Pitt taking on Conservative base, prepared

indicators.note: taking on means admitting something into oneself, so the pieces go inside the actor's name

blocks.note: Brad Pitt the actor
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Pitt, the Tory prime minister, readies himself to address his core voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitt' with 'Conservative' summons William Pitt; it is the actor Brad Pitt.
explanation.definitionFit: To be braced is to be ready for an impact, the same as prepared for it.

clue.text: S African actor taking time off - she's going fishing

indicators.note: taking off means removing, so the abbreviation for time is dropped

blocks.note: Charlize Theron, the South African-born actor
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A South African actress takes a break and goes angling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the actress on holiday; the fishing 'she' is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a wading bird that stands in shallow water to catch fish.

clue.text: Bigoted Blair lie damaged Labour's leader

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a different order
a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded falsehood from Tony Blair hurt the Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour's leader' looks like Blair himself, but it only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal means intolerant of other views, which is close to bigoted.

clue.text: *@!#* British former Prime Minister turned up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, so the name runs backwards

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
Sir Robert Peel, nineteenth-century PM

explanation.surface: Someone swears in shock as an old prime minister appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The string of symbols is how comics print a censored oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is the electronic tone broadcasters use to mask a swear word, as the symbols do in print.

clue.text: 100,000 Indian spicy meatballs Lawrence? Such vulgarity!

blocks.note: a lac or lakh is the Indian term for 100,000
koftas are spiced meatballs from South Asian cooking
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A huge order of curry-house meatballs for someone called Lawrence is deemed crass.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgarity is coarseness or a want of refinement, which is what having no taste means.

clue.text: See 9
Starts to woo anonymous donor for a bundle of cash

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A party courts a secret benefactor in the hope of a large cash gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A wad is a thick roll of banknotes.

clue.text: Alfresco gathering which didn't turn out fine for Johnson?

blocks.note: straight reading: a social event held outdoors

blocks.clueFragment: which didn't turn out fine for Johnson?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a lockdown event in the Downing Street grounds for which Boris Johnson was not fined by police, unlike his birthday gathering

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' suggests sunny weather spoiling an outdoor event, but refers to the Partygate penalty notices; Johnson's one fine was for a birthday gathering indoors, not the May 2020 'bring your own booze' event outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor social function held on a lawn is what alfresco gathering describes.
